recipes.name: Lime Gelatin Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 (6 ounce) package lime flavored Jell-O® mix
1 (20 ounce) can crushed pineapple, drained with juice reserved

steps.text: Combine boiling water and gelatin mix in a large bowl; stir until dissolved. Stir in 1/2 cup pineapple juice. Refrigerate until thickened but not set, about 1 hour.

Meanwhile, place crushed pineapple and remaining juice in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, and simmer for about 5 minutes. Remove from heat, and cool to room temperature. Blend softened cream cheese and prepared gelatin until smooth. Mix in cooled pineapple.
Beat heavy cream in a chilled glass or metal bowl with an electric mixer until soft peaks form.
Fold whipped cream into gelatin mixture. Fold in chopped nuts. Pour into a pretty glass bowl, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or until set.

raw_recipe.headline: Lime Gelatin Salad
raw_recipe.description: This creamy lime jello salad also features crushed pineapple and chopped pecans for a refreshing green dessert that will please any crowd!

review.reviewBody: Very good. Fist time making I thought the prep directions were more than needed to do. So the second time I made it, I dissolved the jello in the hot water, added the cream cheese and beat with mixer. Added the pineapple with juice, and 1/2 cup pecan pieces. Then I folded in the whipped whipping cream. This way it was more simple to prepare and came out great!

Took this to a Christmas get together on my hubby's side & it was a complete hit! Mother in law even asked for recipe as well as 2 others. We served it with the meal, and some chose it for dessert too, (over pumpkin pie). My grandma makes a variation of this with marshmallows, but I prefer this recipe. I recommend it setting overnight for the flavors to blend.
This is a wonderful salad. I made it for the family Christmas buffet and added a layer of red jello to the top for a festive look. It will be a new family tradition.

I've been searching all my cookbooks for this recipe - my grandmother always made this for holiday meals, and I'm so happy to have found it! I found that the gelatin sets up too firmly if left for an hour - 1/2 hour is adequate. Also, I used only a little more than half of the whipping cream and it turned out fine. Molds beautifully!

This has been a tradition at our holiday for years. We leave out the pecans, don't heat the pineapple (our recipe didn't call for that) and sometimes don't whip the cream when short on time. Still turns out great! Oh and an immersion hand blender works beautifully when the jello sets up a little faster than you expected.
 My husband doesn't like pineapple, so I made him a cherry version. Subbed two 4 oz. boxes of sugar-free black cherry jello, upped the boiling water to 1-1/2 c. and added chopped fresh bing cherries. Yum! Could even add chopped almonds to compliment the cherries. Next? Strawberry-banana walnut? The possibilities are up to you!

You don’t have to heat up the pineapple, the bromelain in fresh pineapple will keep jello from setting, but the process of canning heats it up to inactivate the bromelain. So just skip this unnecessary step. Otherwise it’s a good recipe.
Maraschino cherries are a must... they add a beautiful color that's especially nice at Christmas.
My mom used to make this, but it was cottage cheese, not cream cheese, that's the recipe I'm looking for, it also had evaporated milk in it. So Good!

Delicious!! I make this every year during the holidays... friends & family always say "oh noooo, not that green thing again," but it's always the first dish to be finished! I add walnuts instead of pecans. 
Be sure to boil the crushed pineapple! One year I tried to throw in the pineapple without heating it on the saucepan as directed, and the gelatin never solidified. 
This is a great side dish and a big hit at every party gathering

I added 1 cup of fresh shredded coconut. Whipped Philadelphia cream cheese instead of the block. Strauss whole whipping cream from Whole Foods. Put it in a mold. We have several Diabetics so substituted Splenda - 1/2 the amount specified. Let is set overnight. Was a HUGE hit. People went back for thirds! Glad I read that fresh Pineapple would prevent it from setting. The crushed Dole canned was fine. Thanks for the recipe. Passed it on!
We always add finely chopped celery. We have never cooked the pineapple. We put mixture in 13x9 glass pan (not a bowl) and cut in squares to serve like your photo shows.
Wasn't sure about the lime gelatin, but it was a delicious flavor from the usual orange and added a bit of zip to the recipe. will make again.
This has been a family favorite for as long as I can remember. I watched my aunt make it when I was young, and always think of her whenever I make it now.

My aunt has made this since 1965. I started making it in 1975. I used evaporated milk in place of heavy cream. Used small curd cottage cheese in place of cream cheese. Added lemon gelatin with the lime gelatin. Used half the water on the gelatin package. It’s my favorite. It goes great with spiral ham. We eat it every Easter.
Yes I also add in 2 tablespoons of Miracle Whip. My mom never used nuts but I am sure it is good. A family favorite for over 60 years!
My mom made this every Christmas! I make it all the time, but add mixed fruit, marshmallows (while liquid is hot). My fave thing! Thank you for reminding me! Gonna make it this week!

My family has been making this for 60 years. It’s not Thanksgiving without it? However, we changed the lime jello to raspberry or strawberry & we add 2 cups of mini marshmallows. Also we make the recipe a little more simple than this one. Put room temp cream cheese in a bowl and mash with fork. Mix jello with boiling water and pour over cheese. Stir well with fork. The cream cheese will end up in small pieces just by stirring in the hot liquid. Pour in marshmallows, stir. Then add pineapple nuts and liquid heavy whipping cream. Stir well & refrigerate. This is much easier and cuts well for plating.
I've made this without whipping the cream. By just pouring it in at the end and chilling. it makes a very firm, sliceable salad
I have been looking for this re ipe for ages. My Nana makes a very similar one, using chilled evaporated milk in place of the heavy cream. This version tastes just as wonderful as hers!

They say our sense of smell is tied the strongest to our memories but a very close second is our sense of taste. Like so many others I remember this lime pineapple salad from as far back as 60 years! My mom and grandmom would be proud! This recipe is easy to follow. I made one change after reading some of the comments. I too cut the whipping cream in half. I have a new dinner favorite. I had expected leftovers but everyone went back for seconds. Oh well, next time I'll double it! Thank you!
